assertions.name: covariance_epic_phase4_interval_fkg_reframing
assertions.source: Kernel (β=3) sharpened to Cov_β(Σc²,Σln h)≥0 on [2,3] (Griffiths/FKG-type): E_β[C₂] monotone-decreasing on [2,3], Cov_β(C₂,ln f)≤0, Cov_β(Σc²,Σln h)≥0, all verified 40 dps k≤14. Both statistics are explicit box-sums (dimension obstruction sidestepped). No fit; no c_k.

description: Phase 4 of the covariance-kernel proof epic (qou-x631): sharpen the kernel to a compact-interval correlation inequality, by analogy with Fulman's Stein/eigenfunction-drift method. The kernel cov(k)=Σ(f^λ)³ω₃≤0 is H(3)≤0 for H(β)=E_β[C₂]−C(k,2). β=3 lies inside the monotone-decreasing window (E_β[C₂] decreases 2→3→4; only rises 4→5, Phase 1), so the kernel needs only the INTERVAL statement d/dβ E_β[C₂]=Cov_β(C₂,ln f)≤0 on [2,3], integrated from H(2)=0. Since ln f=ln k!−Σln h, this is Cov_β(Σc², Σln h)≥0 on [2,3] — a Griffiths-II/FKG-type POSITIVE correlation between two explicit box-sum statistics (content-spread, log-hook-sum), which sidesteps the dimension-not-polynomial obstruction (dim∉A but Σc², Σln h are explicit box-sums). Verified 40 dps on a fine β-grid over [2,3], all k≤14: (a) E_β[C₂] monotone non-increasing; (b) Cov_β(C₂,ln f)≤0; (c) Cov_β(Σc²,Σln h)≥0. This SHARPENS the open target; it does not close it. scope-(a); no fit; nothing wired; no c_k; L2 2/7.

data.fkg_target: Cov_beta(sum c^2, sum ln h) >= 0 on [2,3]
